title: I Logged Every CSA Pickup Swap My Box Captain Called Overflow

parts.text: I arrived at the church lot at 4:02 p.m. and my share crate was empty except a note: OVERFLOW TO CAPTAIN. The CSA rules laminated on the cooler said: ONE BOX PER SHARE. SWAPS LOGGED. Captain June palmed my tomatoes into a tote labeled extras. I was thirty-six, shareholder, holding a week-19 barcode. "Captains are shares of labor." I photographed the empty crate, the barcode, and the tote. Then I logged a missing-share ticket. At 4:11 the farmer asked why June's name was on my tomatoes. I kept my voice indoor and let the timestamp talk.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The farmer can see June's extras tote on my week-19 barcode.

social.video_title: She moved my tomatoes into an extras tote — Part 1/2
social.description: CSA lot, an empty crate, and a cooler rule she posted. I logged the missing share. Would you have photographed the tote?

parts.text: June called it ripening until the farmer asked for the log. I printed the ticket, the photo, and the barcode. Tomatoes went back. June packed her own labor share and told the line overflow was always about optics. Optics is a word captains use when a tote exists. Pickup now has a second line: CAPTAINS ARE NOT EXTRAS. I keep a labeled crate. June brown-bags. The lot finally looks like a farm, not a pantry. I kept the printout in a folder labeled BORING. I have learned the difference between a title and a line item.

social.description: Missing-share ticket, returned tomatoes, and a second line. Was ripening ever my crate?
